intros.overview: Explore the chip and the complete isometric model of the UNIT PULSAR board. Every chip specification links to the ESP32-C5 Series Datasheet v1.5.
intros.inside: A 240 MHz high-performance RISC-V CPU works alongside a 48 MHz low-power RISC-V CPU. Follow the memory and clock resources that support them.
intros.pins: The board's Nano-style labels and the ESP32-C5's GPIO numbers are different maps. Check both before wiring a circuit.
intros.blocks: Find the ESP32-C5's on-chip interfaces, analog functions, radios and security features, with direct links to the source pages.
intros.read: Read the bundled 96-page ESP32-C5 Series Datasheet v1.5, or open Espressif's online PDF.

overview.boardText: Rotate and inspect all four manufacturing layers. Open the component menu to highlight the MCU, sensors, power system and connectors.
overview.chipBoardTitle: Chip and board are different layers
overview.chipBoardText: The ESP32-C5HR8 provides the RISC-V CPUs, radios and 8 MiB in-package PSRAM. UNIT adds the external 8 MiB QSPI flash, sensors, microSD, battery circuit and connectors on the Pulsar board.

inside.hpTitle: Main RISC-V CPU · up to 240 MHz
inside.hpText: The 32-bit main CPU runs applications and handles the chip's high-performance peripherals and wireless work.
inside.lpTitle: Low-power RISC-V CPU · up to 48 MHz
inside.lpText: A separate 32-bit controller can keep low-power tasks running while the main domain sleeps.
inside.flashTitle: The board also has external flash
inside.flashText: The Pulsar C5 board uses an 8 MiB BY25Q64ES QSPI NOR flash for program storage. This is separate from the ESP32-C5HR8's 8 MiB in-package PSRAM.

pins.twoMapsText: The board map below follows UNIT's Pulsar C5 hardware reference, revision V1.2.3. The chip datasheet describes GPIO capabilities and boot strapping. D2/RGB is GPIO0.
pins.bootNote: GPIO26, GPIO27 and GPIO28 are strapping pins. The board's D3/BOOT label maps to GPIO28; check the boot-state requirements before attaching a circuit.
